dat <- read.csv("/Users/zixinli05/Desktop/Data\ Analysis/combined.csv")

unique(dat$condition)
## [1] "scrambled" "intact"
table(dat$condition, useNA = "ifany")
## 
##    intact scrambled 
##        34        34
dat$condition <- factor(
  dat$condition,
  levels = c("intact", "scrambled")
)

table(dat$condition, useNA = "ifany")
## 
##    intact scrambled 
##        34        34
#Graph 1: mean curves
summary_dat <- dat %>%
  group_by(condition, delay_ms) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_rating = mean(probability_rating, na.rm = TRUE),
    se = sd(probability_rating, na.rm = TRUE) /
      sqrt(sum(!is.na(probability_rating))),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(
  summary_dat,
  aes(
    x = delay_ms,
    y = mean_rating,
    color = condition,
    group = condition
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      ymin = mean_rating - se,
      ymax = mean_rating + se
    ),
    width = 15
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100)) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  labs(
    x = "Temporal delay (ms)",
    y = "Mean causal judgment",
    color = "Condition"
  )

model_dat <- dat %>%
  select(participant, condition, delay_ms, probability_rating) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(participant),
    !is.na(condition),
    !is.na(delay_ms),
    !is.na(probability_rating)
  ) %>%
  droplevels()

str(model_dat)
## 'data.frame':    68 obs. of  4 variables:
##  $ participant       : chr  "s001" "s001" "s001" "s001" ...
##  $ condition         : Factor w/ 2 levels "intact","scrambled": 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 ...
##  $ delay_ms          : int  100 -33 -17 500 1000 33 -750 17 -50 750 ...
##  $ probability_rating: int  37 40 82 56 0 38 0 100 99 19 ...
table(model_dat$condition)
## 
##    intact scrambled 
##        34        34
table(model_dat$participant)
## 
## s001 s002 
##   34   34
model_dat$participant <- factor(model_dat$participant)
model_dat$condition <- factor(model_dat$condition)
model_dat$delay_ms <- as.numeric(model_dat$delay_ms)
model_dat$probability_rating <- as.numeric(model_dat$probability_rating)
levels(model_dat$condition)
## [1] "intact"    "scrambled"
levels(model_dat$participant)
## [1] "s001" "s002"
library(mgcv)

gamm_test <- gam(
  probability_rating ~
    condition +
    s(delay_ms, k = 6) +
    s(participant, bs = "re"),
  data = model_dat,
  method = "REML" 
)

summary(gamm_test)
## 
## Family: gaussian 
## Link function: identity 
## 
## Formula:
## probability_rating ~ condition + s(delay_ms, k = 6) + s(participant, 
##     bs = "re")
## 
## Parametric coefficients:
##                    Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept)          74.000      5.411   13.68  < 2e-16 ***
## conditionscrambled  -25.265      5.875   -4.30 6.16e-05 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Approximate significance of smooth terms:
##                   edf Ref.df     F  p-value    
## s(delay_ms)    3.5080  4.153 7.989 2.41e-05 ***
## s(participant) 0.5821  1.000 1.393    0.127    
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## R-sq.(adj) =  0.433   Deviance explained = 47.6%
## -REML = 308.54  Scale est. = 586.85    n = 68
gamm <- gam(
  probability_rating ~
    condition +
    s(delay_ms, by = condition, k = 6) + #Give each condition its own nonlinear temporal curve.
    s(participant, bs = "re"),
  data = model_dat,
  method = "REML"
)

summary(gamm)
## 
## Family: gaussian 
## Link function: identity 
## 
## Formula:
## probability_rating ~ condition + s(delay_ms, by = condition, 
##     k = 6) + s(participant, bs = "re")
## 
## Parametric coefficients:
##                    Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept)          74.000      5.313  13.927  < 2e-16 ***
## conditionscrambled  -25.265      5.507  -4.588 2.36e-05 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Approximate significance of smooth terms:
##                                   edf Ref.df     F  p-value    
## s(delay_ms):conditionintact    2.0923  2.544 1.737    0.194    
## s(delay_ms):conditionscrambled 3.7517  4.371 9.784 2.47e-06 ***
## s(participant)                 0.6328  1.000 1.723    0.104    
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## R-sq.(adj) =  0.502   Deviance explained = 55.8%
## -REML = 302.69  Scale est. = 515.58    n = 68
gam.check(gamm_test)

## 
## Method: REML   Optimizer: outer newton
## full convergence after 6 iterations.
## Gradient range [-2.078409e-09,1.228064e-10]
## (score 308.5431 & scale 586.8546).
## Hessian positive definite, eigenvalue range [0.1665226,32.55202].
## Model rank =  9 / 9 
## 
## Basis dimension (k) checking results. Low p-value (k-index<1) may
## indicate that k is too low, especially if edf is close to k'.
## 
##                   k'   edf k-index p-value
## s(delay_ms)    5.000 3.508    1.22    0.95
## s(participant) 2.000 0.582      NA      NA
plot(gamm, pages = 1)

gam.check(gamm)

## 
## Method: REML   Optimizer: outer newton
## full convergence after 5 iterations.
## Gradient range [-0.0002159327,6.543239e-07]
## (score 302.6861 & scale 515.5793).
## Hessian positive definite, eigenvalue range [0.1966105,32.07344].
## Model rank =  14 / 14 
## 
## Basis dimension (k) checking results. Low p-value (k-index<1) may
## indicate that k is too low, especially if edf is close to k'.
## 
##                                   k'   edf k-index p-value
## s(delay_ms):conditionintact    5.000 2.092    1.24    0.96
## s(delay_ms):conditionscrambled 5.000 3.752    1.24    0.98
## s(participant)                 2.000 0.633      NA      NA
model_diff <- gam(
  probability_rating ~
    condition +
    s(delay_ms, by = condition, k = 6) +
    s(participant, bs = "re"),
  data = model_dat,
  method = "ML" 
)
model_same <- gam(
  probability_rating ~
    condition +
    s(delay_ms, k = 6) +
    s(participant, bs = "re"),
  data = model_dat,
  method = "ML"
)
#Graph 2, ANOVA Results Table

anova(model_same, model_diff, test = "Chisq") #whether the two-curve model fits significantly better than the shared-curve model. Answer: Yes, the two temporal curves differ in pilot data.
## Analysis of Deviance Table
## 
## Model 1: probability_rating ~ condition + s(delay_ms, k = 6) + s(participant, 
##     bs = "re")
## Model 2: probability_rating ~ condition + s(delay_ms, by = condition, 
##     k = 6) + s(participant, bs = "re")
##   Resid. Df Resid. Dev     Df Deviance Pr(>Chi)  
## 1    60.916      37366                           
## 2    57.925      31837 2.9909   5529.1  0.01475 *
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
# Create prediction data
newdat <- expand.grid(
  delay_ms = seq(
    min(model_dat$delay_ms),
    max(model_dat$delay_ms),
    length.out = 300
  ),
  condition = levels(model_dat$condition),
  participant = NA
)

# Make sure participant has the same factor structure as in the model
newdat$participant <- factor(
  newdat$participant,
  levels = levels(model_dat$participant)
)

# Predict causal judgment
pred <- predict(
  model_diff,
  newdata = newdat,
  se.fit = TRUE
)

# Add predicted values
newdat$fit <- pred$fit
newdat$se <- pred$se.fit

# 95% confidence interval
newdat$lower <- newdat$fit - 1.96 * newdat$se
newdat$upper <- newdat$fit + 1.96 * newdat$se
head(newdat)
##     delay_ms condition participant fit se lower upper
## 1 -1000.0000    intact        <NA>  NA NA    NA    NA
## 2  -993.3110    intact        <NA>  NA NA    NA    NA
## 3  -986.6221    intact        <NA>  NA NA    NA    NA
## 4  -979.9331    intact        <NA>  NA NA    NA    NA
## 5  -973.2441    intact        <NA>  NA NA    NA    NA
## 6  -966.5552    intact        <NA>  NA NA    NA    NA
#predicted results visualization
#1.Create prediction data using an actual participant
levels(model_dat$participant)
## [1] "s001" "s002"
newdat <- expand.grid(
  delay_ms = seq(
    min(model_dat$delay_ms),
    max(model_dat$delay_ms),
    length.out = 300
  ),
  condition = levels(model_dat$condition),
  participant = levels(model_dat$participant)[1]
)

pred <- predict(
  gamm,
  newdata = newdat,
  se.fit = TRUE,
  exclude = "s(participant)"
)
#2.Add the confidence intervals
newdat$fit <- as.numeric(pred$fit)
newdat$se <- as.numeric(pred$se.fit)

newdat$lower <- newdat$fit - 1.96 * newdat$se
newdat$upper <- newdat$fit + 1.96 * newdat$se

summary(newdat$fit)
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
##  -2.319  36.121  63.495  53.010  71.708  79.175
summary(newdat$lower)
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
##  -28.94   15.21   45.12   35.21   56.59   67.63
summary(newdat$upper)
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
##   18.77   56.68   82.02   70.81   86.96   90.89
sum(is.na(newdat$fit))

sum(is.na(newdat$lower))

sum(is.na(newdat$upper))

#Graph 3, predicting the 0–100 causal rating from condition and a nonlinear smooth of temporal delay, with participant as a random effect.
ggplot(
  newdat,
  aes(
    x = delay_ms,
    y = fit,
    color = condition,
    fill = condition
  )
) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(

    ),

  ) +

  ) +

    ),
